results.question: How much is the monthly fee on the everyday account and how do I avoid paying it?
results.answer:
The Everyday Account monthly fee is KES 250. You do not pay the KES 250 monthly fee in any month when either of these is true: your salary is paid into the account that month, or your average balance for the month is KES 50,000 or more.

To avoid it, either of these works:
- The KES 250 monthly fee is waived for any month in which your salary is paid into your Kaskazi Everyday Account.
- Kaskazi Bank adds up the balance in your Kaskazi Everyday Account at the end of each day of the month, then divides by the number of days in the month.

I can also check your recent activity on your Everyday Account if you'd like to see where you stand this month.

results.question: what does 'up to 50 days interest free' actually mean? do I get 50 days on everything I buy with the credit card?
results.answer:
No, you don't get 50 days on everything. It's the longest possible period, and it depends on when in the statement period you buy. A purchase made on the first day of a statement period waits the longest before it is due, so it gets the full 50 days. A purchase made on the last day of a statement period gets the fewest days.

For example, with a statement period from 1 May to 31 May and a payment due date of 20 June, a purchase on 1 May gets 50 days, one on 15 May gets 36 days, and one on 31 May gets 20 days.

Two conditions also apply. The interest-free period applies only when you pay your full statement balance by the payment due date. And it does not apply to cash advances.

- **Credit record:** Missed instalments are recorded on your loan and are reported to credit reference bureaus. A missed instalment can make it harder for you to borrow in future, from us or anyone else.

If you know an instalment will be late, tell us before the instalment date. We cannot always waive the fee, but we can often agree a plan that avoids further missed payments.

results.question: how much is the monthly fee on everyday account? and can i avoid paying it
results.answer:
The monthly fee on the Kaskazi Everyday Account is **KES 250**. Its fees are: Monthly account fee KES 250.

You can avoid it in either of two ways. You do not pay the KES 250 monthly fee in any month when either of these is true: your salary is paid into the account that month, or your average balance for the month is KES 50,000 or more.

For the salary waiver, salary means pay sent to you by your employer. Money you move yourself from another account doesn't count. For the balance waiver, Kaskazi Bank adds up the balance in your Kaskazi Everyday Account at the end of each day of the month, then divides by the number of days in the month. A large deposit near month-end usually won't lift the average enough, so keeping a steady balance is what matters.

results.question: how is the personal loan interest worked out, is it linked to the base rate?

If the Base Rate changes, we recalculate your instalment on the balance you then owe, over the months left in your term, so your loan still ends on the same date. We write to you in the app before the change takes effect, telling you the new rate, your new instalment and the date it starts.

- using any final pay or severance pay to reduce the loan, if you choose
